measured_on: RE-HARVESTED on the venue that matches every other pin file in this repo: a 2-node H100 cluster, Intel Xeon Platinum 8480C + 8x H100 80GB HBM3 SXM5, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0, CLOCKS FREE-RUNNING. ONE SERIAL whole-perf-suite run (CPO_PERF_MEASURE=1 pytest -q -s tests/perf/, 9m52s), never a single-file run -- sustained load moves the free-running clock. The FIRST harvest of these cells was taken on an AMD EPYC 7413 box and is DISCARDED: a dispatch ratio is only venue-portable if the submit path and the bare-GemmSm90 reference scale together, and across that CPU gap they do not. The damage was measurable -- ('workflow',2048,384,'outgoing') harvested 39.98 ms on EPYC against 32.65 ms here, a 22% too-loose pin, and this gate is ONE-SIDED so a loose pin never fails, it just silently stops detecting. Never harvest on an H200 either, for the same one-sided reason.

cells.note: 21.07x a bare GemmSm90 launch at the smallest accepted shape (N_token=8, D=32). Large by design: this is a DISPATCHER -- one call runs the size->config heuristic, builds the config, reshapes/transposes operands into views, and submits FOUR kernels. Read against the per-kernel dispatch pins it composes. Also carries op 7's per-call autotuner key build, which `main` pays too; that cost vanishes at every production cell (6-170 ms) which is exactly why it needs a pin at a shape where it does not.
